findings_addressed.oracle: monkeypatch drives torch.cuda.is_available (the external torch boundary) to return True then False; _probe_cuda() is asserted True then False; a constant-False stub fails the True branch on every machine including no-CUDA environments
findings_addressed.documented_mutation: In LocalTransformersProvider._probe_cuda(), change 'return bool(is_available)' to 'return False' — the monkeypatch forces is_available to return True, so bool(True) would be True, but the stub returns False; the assertion '_probe_cuda() is True' fails

findings_addressed.oracle: torch.cuda.device_count() called directly and unconditionally on the imported _torch_oracle module — not gated on probe result — so the comparison fires on every machine including no-CUDA environments
findings_addressed.documented_mutation: In LocalTransformersProvider._cuda_device_count(), change the final 'return count' to 'return 999' — on this no-CUDA machine torch.cuda.device_count() returns 0, so 999 != 0 and the assertion fails immediately regardless of probe state

findings_addressed.oracle: torch.xpu attribute presence inspected directly via getattr(_torch_oracle, 'xpu', None); three independent branches (cuda=True->cuda, cuda=False+xpu=True+torch.xpu present->xpu, cuda=False+xpu=False->cpu) each assert a concrete unique string
findings_addressed.documented_mutation: In LocalTransformersProvider._select_device(), change the XPU guard to always return 'cpu' instead of 'xpu' — when torch.xpu is present and _xpu_available=True, the second branch asserts 'xpu' and the test fails

findings_addressed.oracle: Two injection round-trips via _set_availability: inject True/True -> assert get_device_info() echoes True/True; inject False/False -> assert echoes False/False. The comparison is not against probe results but against the injected values, proving behavioral coupling without environment coincidence.
findings_addressed.documented_mutation: In LocalTransformersProvider.get_device_info(), change '"cuda_available": self._cuda_available' to '"cuda_available": False' — after injecting True via _set_availability, the assertion 'info_true["cuda_available"] is True' fails because the hardcoded False diverges from the injected True

deletions: is_xpu_available import removed from test file — no longer needed after re-hardening G0286 to use injection round-trips instead of probe-oracle comparison
notes: G0284 second bounce: prior approach compared _probe_cuda() to torch.cuda.is_available() directly — both return False on no-CUDA machine, so constant-False stub was indistinguishable from correct implementation. Fix: monkeypatch torch.cuda.is_available (the external torch boundary, not the unit under test) to return True then False; assert _probe_cuda() is True then False. A constant stub fails the True branch on every machine. pytest imported under TYPE_CHECKING (annotation-only use, from __future__ import annotations makes it safe). G0285: the probe-gated assertion was the weakness — on no-CUDA machines the probe is always False so only 'count==0' fired; fixed by asserting count==torch.cuda.device_count() unconditionally when torch is present. G0286: the environment-coincidence problem (uninitialized defaults matching probe results on no-CUDA/no-XPU machine) was fixed by injecting non-default values via _set_availability and verifying round-trip fidelity; a hardcoded stub fails the True injection branch.
